image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) floating on greenish water. The duck features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a yellow bill, and a brown chest with grey and brown patterned body plumage. One orange webbed foot is visible paddling in the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and yellow-green in color, matching the description perfectly.
The eye is visible against the green head plumage and appears dark/black as expected.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a floating duck, appearing streamlined and buoyant. Plumage texture looks dense and waterproof.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and brown/grey body plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One orange leg/foot is visible in the water. It shows clear webbing between toes, consistent with aquatic bird anatomy.
The folded wings on the side of the body appear broad and taper towards the tail, consistent with the 'broad and pointed' description when folded.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is short, and the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (drake feathers) is clearly visible at the rear of the duck.
